prompt:
Paint the COMPLETE top-down map of one outdoor area of rugged mining mountains in a fantasy JRPG world as ONE finished game map image, in rich premium modern hi-bit pixel art (hand-placed crisp square pixels, hue-shifted colour ramps, dark warm outlines, lush natural detail), classic top-down RPG map view seen from above with a slight 3/4 tilt (tree crowns, rocks and buildings seen from above with their south-facing sides visible; NOT an isometric view, NOT a diorama, no depth-of-field, no tilt-shift, no 3D render, no perspective).

THE PLACE: A MINING VALLEY in the Gard mountains, enclosed by high grey-brown cliffs: in the middle of the north cliff the great GATE of an underground mining town, huge timber-and-iron double doors under a carved stone lintel with an anvil emblem, flanked by two tall timber watchtowers; a cold clear mountain stream comes down from the north-east and winds south-west across the valley under timber bridges; grey slag heaps and heaps of ore; an open ore-sorting shed with a slate roof on timber posts; a mine-cart rail track leads from beside the gate east along the valley; gravel roads, alpine grass, heather, firs on the slopes. Palette: slate greys, umbers, iron and timber browns, muted greens, cold blue water. Busy-looking but quiet, a working valley.

The FIRST attached image is an exact LAYOUT GUIDE drawn on a 54 x 40 tile grid (each tile = 48 x 48 px of the output; the output is 2592 x 1920 px). Trace over it: your painting is laid pixel-for-pixel on top of it and used directly as the walkable game map, so every road, rail, shore, cliff, wall, tree mass, water body and landmark must sit exactly where it is in the guide at the same size (keep every edge within a few pixels of the guide; do not shift, shrink, mirror or re-arrange anything; keep the exact width of the roads and of the one- and two-tile gaps).

The SECOND attached image is only a STYLE REFERENCE from the same game: match its pixel-art rendering (pixel size, clusters, outlines, colour ramps, level of detail). Do NOT copy anything from it (no objects, signs or buildings from it).

The guide is soft colour-coding only (its blurred edges only mean the edge is natural and free-flowing): do NOT copy its flat colours, straight tile steps, circles, triangles or stripes. Interpret every area as the real material with rich natural variation, and give cliffs, rock walls, streams and meadows natural, organic, slightly irregular outlines (bulging or receding by at most a third of a tile around the guide edge). Make it feel like a real, exciting place to explore, full of small natural detail.

Guide colour key:
- green = short ALPINE GRASS (walkable, flat): tough mountain turf with small stones, moss and tiny white and yellow flowers.
- olive with short strokes = HEATHER and tall mountain grass (walkable, low, flat).
- green with small pink/white dots = MOUNTAIN FLOWERS in the grass (walkable).
- light tan band = the GRAVEL ROAD: packed grey-brown gravel and cart ruts, small stones along its edges (walkable).
- darker brown = a narrow FOOTPATH of trodden earth (walkable).
- white with pale blue arcs = patches of OLD SNOW and loose scree (walkable, flat).
- grey with arcs = FLAT ROCK SHELVES (walkable): level bare grey rock, cracks and lichen, level with the ground around it.
- brown with steel lines = a RAIL TRACK for mine carts (walkable): dark wooden sleepers across, two steel rails along the line, gravel ballast.
- brown with plank lines = WOODEN PLANKS of a bridge / trestle / boardwalk (walkable deck).
- light blue = a shallow FORD of the stream (walkable): clear water over pebbles.
- blue = a mountain STREAM or pool (not walkable): clear cold water over stones, white riffles.
- dark blue = deep water (not walkable).
- dark green triangles = CONIFERS (not walkable): dark fir and spruce seen from above, their crowns overlapping into dark masses.
- round green-olive blobs = DWARF PINES and bushes (not walkable).
- grey circles = BOULDERS, ore heaps and slag heaps (not walkable).
- all colour areas are LEVEL GROUND unless listed as not walkable; only the cliffs below are raised.
- grey-brown with horizontal strata and a green top edge = MOUNTAIN CLIFFS / rock faces (not walkable): sheer layered grey-brown rock, cracked ledges, grass overhanging the top edge, scree at the foot; their outlines are natural and rounded, never square or stepped.
- black = a deep CHASM (not walkable): a sheer drop into darkness.
Landmarks (paint each exactly on its block, at the block's size):
- the blocks in colour rgb(92,70,52) = the great GATE of the cavern town: a tall arched opening cut into the cliff, closed by huge double doors of dark timber bound with iron, a carved stone lintel with an anvil emblem above.
- small BLACK rectangles = the front DOORS / openings. Paint each door exactly at that spot and size (a wooden door or a dark opening, its bottom edge on the bottom edge of the wall). Do not add any other door or opening that looks like a door.
- the blocks in colour rgb(140,100,62) = a tall square timber WATCHTOWER on stone footings with a small shingled roof.
- the blocks in colour rgb(140,100,62) = a tall square timber WATCHTOWER on stone footings with a small shingled roof.
- the blocks in colour rgb(104,96,92) = an open ORE-SORTING SHED: a slate roof on thick timber posts over wooden sorting tables and heaps of grey ore.
Walkable areas must stay walkable-looking: no boulders, trees, fences, crates, carts or objects standing on them unless the guide shows them.

Pixel art rules: crisp square pixels, no blur, no anti-aliasing, no painterly brush strokes, no noise, clear clusters, hue-shifted ramps. Characters in this game are about 72 output px tall, so details should be at that scale.
Lighting: this is the ALBEDO base layer (the game darkens it into night at runtime and adds lamp light on top). Neutral, soft, even daylight-like light as in the style reference; NO darkness, NO night tint, NO long cast shadows, NO light pools, NO glow halo, NO vignette, NO fog over the map, NO clouds over the map.
Do NOT paint any characters, people, animals, monsters, birds, mine carts on the rails, treasure chests, lanterns, lamp posts, torches, campfires, signs, signposts, text, letters, numbers, labels, grid lines, borders, frames or UI. Those are added later as separate sprites: leave the ground open for them.
revised_prompt: Create ONE complete finished 2592×1920 top-down JRPG game map by EDITING/painting DIRECTLY OVER the FIRST attached 54×40-tile layout image, retaining its exact geometry, landmark coordinates, widths and walkability. The SECOND attached image is strictly a pixel-art STYLE reference, never a layout or object reference. Output only image, with no borders, text or grid. Maintain near-pixel-perfect registration with the first image: all edges and objects correspond to its existing positions, especially the northern cliff boundary, central northern cavern gate and its two flanking towers, main road winding from west through center to east and climbing north to gate, stream entering upper-right and winding southwest to lower-left, two road/rail wooden bridges across it, eastward rail course, ore shed upper-right of gate, stands of firs and discrete ore heaps, southern mountain-cliff boundary. Strictly preserve the clear narrow gaps between objects, the road widths, bridges and stream width, and do not place any obstructing props on grassy walkable areas or roads. The flat gray-brown perimeter at top and bottom represents huge natural stratified mountain cliffs with rounded green overhanging rim, fissures, strata and scree; do not interpret it as a flat plain. The brown block at top center is an immense arched cliff-cut gate with massive shut dark timber-and-iron double doors, stone lintel with carved ANVIL pictogram; small black rectangle at its southern edge is the door opening; the two little brown blocks on either side are tall square timber watchtowers on stone bases, shingled roofs. Gray rectangular block upper center-right is the slate-roofed open ore-sorting shed with posts, sorting tables and ore beneath. Trace pale central meandering band as packed gravel road, diagonal brown band eastward as narrow mining rail with iron rails and dark sleepers, brown plank bands over water as timber bridges. Flowing cold blue river with stones and sparkling white ripples. Alpine green grasses, heather, small mountain flowers, spruce/fir masses on exactly indicated patches, organically shaped boulder and slag-heap masses at gray round clusters. No extra structures/doors, characters, vehicles, lamps, signs, UI, lettering or grid. Rich premium modern HI-BIT HAND-PLACED PIXEL ART with crisp square pixel clusters, warm dark outlines, carefully hue-shifted shadow and highlight ramps, intricate natural surface texture and distinct materials, matching the second image's rendering density and pixel scale. Classic overhead RPG with south-facing sides visible, NOT isometric or perspective. Soft neutral uniform daylight albedo, no vignette, glow, haze, cast shadows, 3D, anti-aliasing or blur. Turn the guide's schematic symbols into realistic natural-shaped forms while keeping their positions and overall footprint exact.
